voiceover: Saw an objection online? It has been asked before. For two thousand years the hard questions have been asked — and answered in writing. In the second century a philosopher named Celsus wrote a full-length attack on the Christian faith. Origen answered him, point by point, across eight books — and quoted him so fully that most of what Celsus wrote survives only inside the reply. Every generation brings its hardest question. In every generation someone answers it in writing. So here is what Asked and Answered does. Paste the tweet. Paste the screenshot. Or just ask the question in your own words. You get a clear answer, in plain language. When the objection has a name on it, you get the person who pressed it — often centuries before you saw it. And you get where to read further, if you want the long version. Recording an objection is not the same as answering it well. Both are on the record. Bring the objection you saw. You are not the first to ask.
